question: 'Dashain' and 'Tihar' are popular festivals of which neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dashain" and "Tihar" are the two biggest and most popular festivals of Nepal. Dashain (like Dussehra) celebrates the victory of good over evil, and Tihar (like Diwali, the festival of lights) is celebrated over five days. (नेपाल के त्योहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dashain is the longest and most auspicious Nepali festival, honouring the goddess Durga.

• Tihar (also called Deepawali/Yamapanchak) worships crows, dogs, cows and includes "Bhai Tika" for brothers and sisters.

NOTE

• Nepal shares a long open border with India; its capital is Kathmandu and its currency is the Nepalese Rupee. Mount Everest lies on the Nepal–China border.

question: Right of a prisoner to speedy trial will be categorised in which of the following Fundamental Rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The right of a prisoner to a speedy trial is a part of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21 (i.e., the Right to Life). The Supreme Court has held (in cases like *Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar*) that a speedy trial is an essential part of Article 21. (अनुच्छेद 21 — जीवन का अधिकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 21 guarantees that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by a procedure established by law.

• Rights read into Article 21 include: speedy trial, free legal aid, privacy, clean environment, and right to education.

NOTE

• The six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

question: All natural earthquakes take place in the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lithosphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All natural earthquakes take place in the "lithosphere" — the rigid, outer layer of the Earth comprising the crust and the uppermost solid mantle. This is where rocks fracture and tectonic plates move, releasing seismic energy. (स्थलमंडल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• An earthquake is the shaking of the Earth's surface caused by the sudden release of energy along a fault.

• The point of origin inside the Earth is the focus (hypocentre); the point directly above on the surface is the epicentre.

NOTE

• Earth's spheres: Lithosphere (land), Hydrosphere (water), Atmosphere (air), Biosphere (life). The asthenosphere is the semi-molten layer below the lithosphere. Earthquakes are measured by the Richter scale/moment magnitude scale using a seismograph.

question: In which of the following years did Alexander invade Punjab and in which of the following years did he die?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 326 BC and 323 BC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alexander the Great invaded Punjab (India) in 326 BC and died in 323 BC (at Babylon). (सिकंदर — आक्रमण 326 ईसा पूर्व, मृत्यु 323 ईसा पूर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In 326 BC, Alexander fought the famous Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) against King Porus (Puru), a ruler of Punjab.

• Impressed by Porus's bravery, Alexander restored his kingdom. His army refused to advance further at the Beas (Vipasha) river.

NOTE

• Alexander was a king of Macedonia, taught by the philosopher Aristotle. His invasion opened land and sea routes between India and the West.

question: In which of the following states is Aoleang Monyü celebrated, which is an ancient spring festival celebrated by all Konyaks in the month of April?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aoleang Monyü" is an ancient spring festival celebrated in April by the Konyak Naga tribe of Nagaland to welcome the new year and seek blessings for a good harvest. (नागालैंड — कोन्याक जनजाति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Konyaks are the largest Naga tribe, historically known as the "head-hunters", living mainly in the Mon district of Nagaland.

• The festival features traditional songs, dances and feasts spread over several days.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Nagaland: Hornbill Festival (the "Festival of Festivals", held in December at Kisama), Moatsu (Ao tribe) and Sekrenyi (Angami tribe).

question: Which of the following is an example of a private sector Industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tata Iron and Steel Company.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO/Tata Steel)" is an example of a private sector industry — it is owned and managed by private individuals/companies (the Tata Group), not the government. (निजी क्षेत्र का उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• LIC, BHEL and SAIL are all public sector undertakings (PSUs) owned and controlled by the Government of India.

• TISCO was founded by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata and set up at Jamshedpur in 1907.

NOTE

• Public sector = government-owned (e.g., ONGC, SAIL, BHEL); Private sector = privately owned (e.g., Tata, Reliance, Infosys); Joint sector = jointly owned by government and private parties.

question: Which specific chemical can be applied to achieve staining of chromosomes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetocarmine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acetocarmine" is a common stain used to colour chromosomes (and the nucleus) so that they can be clearly observed under a microscope, especially during cell division (mitosis/meiosis). (एसीटोकारमीन — गुणसूत्र अभिरंजन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other nuclear/chromosome stains include aceto-orcein, Feulgen stain and Giemsa stain.

• Staining increases the contrast between cell structures and the background, making them visible.

NOTE

• Ethanol and methanol are used as fixatives (to preserve tissue), and hydrochloric acid is used in hydrolysis for the Feulgen reaction — not as the direct chromosome stain.

question: Which chronicler of the medieval age recognised that Raziyya was more able and qualified than all her brothers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Minhaj-i-Siraj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The medieval chronicler "Minhaj-i-Siraj" (Minhaj-us-Siraj) recognised that Razia Sultan was more able and qualified than all her brothers, though he was troubled that she was a woman ruler. (मिन्हाज-ए-सिराज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Minhaj-i-Siraj wrote the famous chronicle "Tabaqat-i-Nasiri", a history of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Razia Sultan (r. 1236–1240) was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, daughter of Iltutmish.

NOTE

• Razia belonged to the Slave/Mamluk dynasty founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. Iltutmish nominated her as his successor over his sons.

question:
If after being bitten by a mosquito, the person is detected as being malaria positive, which of the following will hold true?

A. The person did not have a balanced diet.
B. The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.
C. The mosquito was suffering from malaria.
D. The person was not vaccinated as a child.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B. The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite "Plasmodium", which is transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. So if a person becomes malaria positive after a bite, statement B — "The mosquito was carrying plasmodium" — must be true. (मलेरिया — प्लाज्मोडियम परजीवी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The mosquito acts only as a carrier/vector; it does not "suffer" from malaria (so statement C is wrong).

• Malaria has nothing to do with diet or childhood vaccination (statements A and D are wrong); there was no widely used routine malaria vaccine at that time.

NOTE

• Malaria species: Plasmodium vivax, P. falciparum (most dangerous), P. malariae, P. ovale. World Malaria Day is observed on 25 April.

question: Which of the following Indian tribal dances is prevalent in the Araku Valley near Visakhapatnam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhimsa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dhimsa" is a popular tribal dance performed in the Araku Valley near Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. It is performed mainly by tribal women in colourful costumes, especially during festivals. (धिम्सा नृत्य — आंध्र प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bagurumba is a folk dance of the Bodo tribe of Assam.

• Jhumur is a folk dance of the tea-garden communities of Assam/West Bengal.

• Bardo Chham is a folk dance of the Sherdukpen tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.

NOTE

• The Araku Valley is a scenic hill station in the Eastern Ghats, famous for its coffee plantations and tribal culture.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution has provisions for the appointment of High Court Judges?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 217.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Article 217" of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment and conditions of the office of a Judge of a High Court. High Court judges are appointed by the President after consultation with the CJI, the Governor of the state, and the Chief Justice of that High Court. (अनुच्छेद 217 — उच्च न्यायालय न्यायाधीश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 214 — High Courts for states.

• Article 216 — constitution of High Courts.

• A High Court judge holds office until the age of 62 years (Supreme Court judges retire at 65).

NOTE

• Article 124 deals with the appointment of Supreme Court judges. Judges are now appointed through the Collegium system.

question: Which of the following is NOT the principle laid down by the OECD about budgetary governance?
option_1: It does not allow the citizen to participate in budgetary debates.
option_2: The execution of the budget must be proactively planned, managed, and monitored.
option_3: Design the capital budgeting framework to meet national development needs.
option_4: Alignment of budgets with medium-term strategic priorities of the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It does not allow the citizen to participate in budgetary debates.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) principles of budgetary governance promote openness, transparency and public participation. Therefore, a statement saying it "does not allow citizens to participate" is NOT an OECD principle — it contradicts the OECD's emphasis on inclusive, participatory budgeting. (ओईसीडी — बजटीय शासन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (proactive budget execution, a sound capital budgeting framework, and aligning budgets with medium-term priorities) ARE genuine OECD principles of good budgetary governance.

NOTE

• The OECD is headquartered in Paris, France, and is often called a group of the world's developed/high-income economies working on economic policy.

question: In February 2024, who was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ritu Bahri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2024, Justice Ritu Bahri was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court. (न्यायमूर्ति ऋतु बाहरी — उत्तराखंड उच्च न्यायालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Uttarakhand High Court is located at Nainital; it was established in the year 2000 when the state was created.

• The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President in consultation with the CJI and the Governor.

NOTE

• India's first woman High Court judge was Justice Anna Chandy; the first woman Supreme Court judge was Justice Fathima Beevi; the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court was Justice Leila Seth.

question: Which of the following countries won the maximum number of T20 Women's Cricket World Cup titles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Australia" has won the maximum number of ICC Women's T20 World Cup titles, dominating the tournament with multiple championships (including 2010, 2012, 2014, 2018, 2020 and 2023). (ऑस्ट्रेलिया — महिला टी20 विश्व कप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ICC Women's T20 World Cup began in 2009, when England won the first edition.

• The West Indies won it once (in 2016).

NOTE

• The Australian women's cricket team is the most successful side in women's cricket, having won multiple ODI World Cups and T20 World Cups.

question: Which of the following Acts provided for a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Trade Disputes Act, 1929.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Trade Disputes Act, 1929" provided for a system of tribunals (Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation) to settle industrial disputes and imposed a ban on strikes in certain public utility services. (ट्रेड डिस्प्यूट्स अधिनियम, 1929)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• During the passing of this Act, the revolutionaries Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly (8 April 1929) in protest against this and the Public Safety Bill.

• Their aim was "to make the deaf hear".

NOTE

• The Age of Consent Act, 1891 raised the age of consent for marriage; the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 governs partnership firms.

question: Which of the following fields is NOT covered by the National Eminence Award?
option_4: Music of all forms and origin
solution_text:
The correct answer is Literature.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, "Literature" is NOT a field covered by the National Eminence Award (Sangeet Natak Akademi's eminence recognition), which focuses on performing arts such as theatre, dance and music. (साहित्य — शामिल नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fields like theatre, dance, and music of all forms and origin fall under the performing arts recognised by such awards.

• Literature is recognised separately by bodies like the Sahitya Akademi.

NOTE

• India's three national academies: Sangeet Natak Akademi (music, dance, drama), Sahitya Akademi (literature) and Lalit Kala Akademi (fine arts).

question: Carnatic singer Bombay Jayashri has been selected for which music award in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangita Kalanidhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The renowned Carnatic vocalist Bombay Jayashri was selected for the prestigious "Sangita Kalanidhi" award for the year 2023, conferred by the Music Academy, Chennai (Madras). (संगीत कलानिधि — बॉम्बे जयश्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Sangita Kalanidhi is one of the highest honours in Carnatic (classical) music.

• Bombay Jayashri is also known for the Oscar-nominated song "Pi's Lullaby" from the film *Life of Pi*.

NOTE

• The Music Academy, Chennai, also confers the "Nritya Kalanidhi" award for excellence in classical dance.

question: Epic Poem, Savitri, described by its author as 'A Legend and a Symbol', was written by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurobindo Ghosh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The epic poem "Savitri — A Legend and a Symbol" was written by Sri Aurobindo (Aurobindo Ghosh). It is one of the longest epic poems in the English language, based on the story of Satyavan and Savitri from the Mahabharata. (श्री अरबिंदो घोष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sri Aurobindo was a freedom fighter, philosopher, yogi and poet; he later founded the Sri Aurobindo Ashram at Puducherry.

• His other works include *The Life Divine* and *Essays on the Gita*.

NOTE

• Sri Aurobindo was associated with the Alipore Bomb Case (1908). His birthday, 15 August, coincides with India's Independence Day.

question: iGOT Karmayogi is an integrated online training platform to provide continuous learning opportunities to ______________ in order to upgrade their skills.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Individual Civil Service Officials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "iGOT Karmayogi" is an integrated online training platform designed to provide continuous learning and skill upgradation to civil service officials (government employees) across India. (आईगॉट कर्मयोगी — सिविल सेवा अधिकारी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is a part of the "Mission Karmayogi" — the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB), launched in 2020.

• The aim is to create a future-ready, professional and citizen-centric civil service.

NOTE

• Mission Karmayogi shifts training from a "rules-based" to a "roles-based" approach, focusing on competency-building of government officials.

question: 'Once a Dancer' is the autobiography of ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allegra Kent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Once a Dancer" is the autobiography of Allegra Kent, a celebrated American ballet dancer of the New York City Ballet. (एलेग्रा केंट की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Allegra Kent was one of the leading ballerinas trained under the famous choreographer George Balanchine.

• The book gives an account of her life and career in classical ballet.

NOTE

• Autobiographies of other dancers: Yamini Krishnamurthy wrote "A Passion for Dance"; Sudha Chandran is known for the film "Nache Mayuri" based on her life.

question: Which track and field event has a water jump?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Steeplechase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Steeplechase" is a track and field event that includes a "water jump" — runners must clear fixed barriers and a water pit placed on the track. The standard distance is 3000 metres. (स्टीपलचेज़ — जल बाधा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In a 3000 m steeplechase, athletes cross 28 barriers and 7 water jumps during the race.

• It tests both endurance and hurdling ability.

NOTE

• Decathlon is a combined event of 10 track and field disciplines; hurdles involve jumping over barriers but no water. India's Avinash Sable is a well-known steeplechase athlete.

question: JJ Thomson is known for developing which model in 1898?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Plum pudding model.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• J. J. Thomson proposed the "Plum pudding model" of the atom (around 1898–1904). According to it, the atom is a sphere of positive charge with negatively charged electrons embedded in it, like plums in a pudding. (प्लम पुडिंग मॉडल — जे.जे. थॉमसन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• J. J. Thomson discovered the electron (1897) using cathode ray experiments and won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1906).

• The "Gold foil model" and nuclear model came from Ernest Rutherford; the "Oil drop experiment" was by R. A. Millikan.

NOTE

• Order of atomic models: Dalton → Thomson (plum pudding) → Rutherford (nuclear) → Bohr → Quantum mechanical model.

question: Who excavated the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila?
solution_text:
The correct answer is John Marshall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sir John Marshall excavated the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila (Takshashila). He conducted extensive archaeological work at Taxila over many years. (जॉन मार्शल — तक्षशिला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• John Marshall was the Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and, in 1924, announced the discovery of the Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa and Mohenjo-daro).

• Taxila was an ancient centre of learning and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site in present-day Pakistan.

NOTE

• Alexander Cunningham is regarded as the "Father of Indian Archaeology" and was the first Director-General of the ASI (founded 1861).

question: The Zaskar and the Nubra are tributaries of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Zaskar" and the "Nubra" are tributaries of the "Indus River". They flow through the Ladakh region and join the Indus. (सिंधु नदी की सहायक नदियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through Ladakh into Pakistan, ending in the Arabian Sea.

• Its major tributaries include the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej, along with the Zaskar, Nubra, Shyok and Gilgit.

NOTE

• The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) between India and Pakistan (brokered by the World Bank) governs the sharing of the Indus and its tributaries. The Indus is the national river of Pakistan.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the population density of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 382/km2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the population density of India was 382 persons per square kilometre. (जनसंख्या घनत्व — 382 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Population density = total population ÷ total land area.

• As per Census 2011, Bihar was the most densely populated state (1106/km²), and Arunachal Pradesh the least dense (17/km²). Delhi was the most densely populated UT.

NOTE

• Census 2011 key figures: total population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%. The census slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". The 2011 census was the 15th national census.
